topics: 🐘 Saddled or Not — resolving the elephant, and names whose letters spell miracles
📿 Mitzvot in Dreams — tefillin, prayer, Shema, and the surprising readings of forbidden unions
🌾 Grain, Fruit, and Field — wheat, barley, vines, figs, pomegranates, olives, dates, goats, myrtle, etrog, lulav
🏞️ The Marsh and the Forest — Rav Pappa, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, and the drum that made a rosh yeshiva
📚 Threes and Sixtieths — kings, prophets, books, sages; fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, dream
🏛️ Blessings on Sights — Mercury, uprooted idolatry, and Rav Hamnuna's five blessings on Babylonia

overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Dream Dictionary and the Five Blessings on Babylonia
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 57a–57b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The first amud is a dictionary of dream images, each keyed to a verse or a wordplay: tefillin promise greatness, barley means sins are removed, a goose means wisdom, a snake means livelihood, a marsh means a yeshiva. Sages report their own dreams — Rabbi Zeira would not leave Babylonia until he saw barley; Rav Ashi dreamed of a drum in a marsh and became head of the yeshiva. The second amud sorts figures and books into triads (piety, wisdom, calamity), lists things that are one-sixtieth of their ideal, and gives medical lists for the sick. Finally, the Gemara returns to the mishna's blessings on sights: on Mercury, on a place cleared of idolatry, and Rav Hamnuna's five blessings for one who sees wicked Babylonia.

slides.title: 🌾 The Dream Dictionary: Image, Meaning, Source
slides.subtitle: How the Gemara reads produce, animals, and actions through verses and wordplay
rows: Tefillin on your head
Expect greatness
'All the peoples shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you' (Deut. 28:10) — Rabbi Eliezer the Great: the head tefillin
Wheat / barley
Peace / your sins are removed
'Fat of wheat' with 'peace' (Ps. 147:14); se'orim = sar avon (Isa. 6:7). Rabbi Zeira waited for barley before leaving Babylonia
A laden vine / a fig / pomegranates
Your wife will not miscarry / your Torah is preserved / business grows like seeds
Ps. 128:3; Prov. 27:18; slices mean Torah for a scholar, mitzvot for an am ha'aretz (Song 4:3, 8:2)
Olives / olive oil / dates
Durable business (trees: many children) / light of Torah / your sins have ended
Ps. 128:3; Ex. 27:20; temarim as tam — 'your iniquity is finished' (Lam. 4:22)
Etrog / lulav / myrtle
Honored (hadur) before your Creator / one heart for your Father / property prospers
Lev. 23:40; lulav as lo lev; Ulla: myrtle only on its stem
Goose / rooster / eggs
Wisdom (relations with it: head of yeshiva — Rav Ashi's own dream) / a son / a pending request; broken: granted
'Wisdoms cry aloud in the streets' (Prov. 1:20); beya = request; also nuts, cucumbers, glass
A snake
Livelihood ready; bit you: doubled; killed it: lost
Rav Sheshet said killing it doubles it — but only because he had killed a snake in his own dream
Wine
The one drink that can go either way
'Wine gladdens the heart' (Ps. 104:15) vs. 'wine unto the bitter in soul' (Prov. 31:6); Rabbi Yoḥanan: for a scholar always good (Prov. 9:5)

callout.label: Also:
callout.text: Answering 'may His great name be blessed' in a dream assures a place in the World-to-Come; reciting Shema means one is worthy of the Divine Presence, but the generation is not. Praying is a good sign only if the dreamer had not yet finished.

slides.title: 🏞️ Marsh, Forest, and Drum: Which Dream Makes a Rosh Yeshiva?
slides.subtitle: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua each dreamed, and each was appointed

nodes.content: 🌿 Baraita: one who enters a marsh (agam) becomes head of a yeshiva — reeds large and small surround him like students. One who enters a forest becomes head of the advanced students (benei kalla) — only great trees around him

columns.label: Version 1
columns.content: Rav Pappa dreamed of a marsh and became rosh yeshiva; Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua dreamed of a forest and became head of the kalla

columns.label: Version 2
columns.content: Both entered a marsh; Rav Pappa also had a drum hanging from his neck — the voice sounded in public — and so he became rosh yeshiva

nodes.content: 🥁 Rav Ashi: I entered a marsh, hung a drum, and beat it — and he became head of the yeshiva

🏠 Other ascents: climbing to a roof means greatness; Abaye and Rava say once he went up, he went up, even if he came down. Entering a city: desires fulfilled (Ps. 107:30). A small boat riding high: a good name; a large boat: for the whole family

🔓 Tearing clothes: the sentence is torn. Naked in Babylonia: free of sin; naked in Eretz Yisrael: bare of mitzvot. Seized by a soldier: heavenly protection; a neck-chain (kolar) adds more — but a mere rope does not

callout.label: Bloodletting:
callout.text: The tanna before Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak taught it means sins are forgiven; the baraita saying sins are 'arranged' (סְדוּרִין) means arranged to be forgiven.

slides.title: 📚 Triads: Piety, Wisdom, or Calamity
slides.subtitle: The Sages sort kings, prophets, books, and scholars into three outcomes

boxes.title: Fear Calamity (פּוּרְעָנוּת)
items: Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha, one of the ten martyrs

callout.label: Outside the pattern:
callout.text: The book of Kings means greatness, Isaiah means consolation, Esther means a miracle, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya means wealth. Rabbi Yoḥanan adds: a verse that falls into one's mouth on waking is a minor prophecy. Seeing Huna hints at a miracle (nes — one nun); Ḥanina, Ḥananya, Yoḥanan: miracles upon miracles (two nuns).

slides.title: 🔢 Five, Six, and Ten: The Mnemonic Lists
slides.subtitle: The Gemara moves from dreams to the body, the sick, and what is one-sixtieth of its ideal

steps.content: 1️⃣ Exceptions: all animals are good except elephant, monkey, and long-tailed ape (an elephant is good when saddled); all metals except hoe, chisel, axe on their handles; all fruit except unripe dates; all vegetables except turnip heads — Rav grew rich after seeing them, but on their stems; all colors except tekhelet; all birds except night-birds

2️⃣ Three enter the body without benefit: cherries, bad dates, unripe dates. Three benefit without entering: washing, anointing, tashmish. Three taste of the World-to-Come: Shabbat, sun, tashmish — meaning relieving oneself, since relations weaken the body
3️⃣ Three ease the mind: voice, sight, smell. Three broaden it: a beautiful home, wife, and vessels
4️⃣ Five are one-sixtieth: fire of Gehenna, honey of manna, Shabbat of the World-to-Come, sleep of death, and a dream of prophecy
5️⃣ Six good signs for the sick: sneezing (Job 41:10), sweat (Gen. 3:19), diarrhea (Isa. 51:14), seminal emission (Isa. 53:10), sleep (Job 3:13), a dream (Isa. 38:16)

6️⃣ Six cures: cabbage, beets, dried foley, stomach, placenta, diaphragm; some add small fish. Ten cause relapse: ox meat, fat, roast, poultry, roasted egg, shaving, cress, milk, cheese, bathhouse; some add nuts and cucumbers — large ones are 'as hard as swords', small ones graced the tables of Rabbi and Antoninus

callout.label: A corpse in the house:
callout.text: Peace for the house; if it ate and drank, a good sign; if it took vessels, a bad sign — Rav Pappa: only a shoe or sandal. Whatever a corpse takes is fine except shoe and sandal; whatever it gives is fine except dust and mustard.

slides.title: 🏛️ Back to the Mishna: Blessings on Idols and on Babylonia
slides.subtitle: The Tosefta on uprooted idolatry, and Rav Hamnuna's five blessings

lines.speaker: Tosefta
lines.text: One who sees Mercury (Markulis) says: Blessed… Who has shown patience to those who violate His will. One who sees a place cleared of idolatry says: Blessed… Who uprooted idolatry from our land — and may it be uprooted from all places of Israel, and turn the hearts of their worshippers to serve You.

lines.speaker: Tosefta
lines.text: Outside the Land one need not say 'turn the hearts of their worshippers', since most inhabitants are gentiles.

lines.speaker: R' Shimon b. Elazar
lines.text: Even outside the Land one must say it, for they are destined to convert: 'Then I will turn to the peoples a pure language' (Zephaniah 3:9).

lines.speaker: Rav Hamnuna
lines.text: One who sees wicked Babylonia must recite five blessings: on its ruins, Who destroyed wicked Babylonia; on Nebuchadnezzar's house, Who destroyed his house; on the lions' den or the furnace, Who did miracles for our fathers in this place; on Mercury, Who shows patience; on a place from which earth is taken, Who speaks and acts, decrees and fulfills.

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: Seeing donkeys carrying earth from Babylonia, he slapped their backs: 'Run, righteous ones, to do the will of your Master!'

lines.speaker: Mar b. Ravina
lines.text: On reaching Babylonia he took earth in his kerchief and threw it outside — 'I will sweep it with the broom of destruction' (Isaiah 14:23).

lines.speaker: Rav Ashi
lines.text: I never heard Rav Hamnuna's teaching, but on my own reasoning I recited all of them.

callout.label: Turning point:
callout.text: The chapter has been about dreams since 55a; here it returns to the mishna's list of sights that call for a blessing, which continues on the next daf.

summary.principle: A dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy: its images are read through Scripture and wordplay, and its readings are confirmed by the sages' own careers.

flowSteps.content: 🐘 The elephant is resolved: saddled is a good omen, unsaddled is not; names with a nun spell miracles
🌾 The dictionary: tefillin → greatness; barley → sins removed; goose → wisdom; snake → livelihood; wine → ambiguous except for scholars
🏞️ Marsh → rosh yeshiva, forest → head of the kalla; Rav Pappa, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, and Rav Ashi's drum

columns.content: 📚 Triads: David/Psalms/Song of Songs/Ben Azzai → piety; Solomon/Ezekiel/Proverbs/Rabbi/Ben Zoma → wisdom; Ahab/Jeremiah/Job/Lamentations/R' Yishmael/Aḥer → calamity
🔢 Five one-sixtieths, six good signs for the sick, six cures, ten causes of relapse

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rav Hamnuna — one who sees wicked Babylonia recites five blessings; Rav Ashi reached them by reasoning alone

quiz.q: How does the Gemara reconcile 'one who sees an elephant will have wonders done for him' with the baraita excluding elephants from good animal dreams?
o: A single elephant is good, many are bad
A saddled elephant is a good omen, an unsaddled one is not
An elephant is good only for a Torah scholar
An elephant is good only in Eretz Yisrael
quiz.e: The Gemara answers 'not difficult': the favorable statement refers to a saddled elephant, the unfavorable one to an elephant that is not saddled.

quiz.q: Why did Rabbi Zeira delay his ascent from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael?
o: Until he dreamed of entering a marsh
Until he saw barley in a dream, a sign that his sins were removed
Until he saw wheat in a dream, a sign of peace
Until he received permission from the exilarch
quiz.e: Barley (se'orim) is read as sar avon, 'your iniquity is taken away' (Isaiah 6:7); Rabbi Zeira said he did not go up until he saw barley in his dream.

quiz.q: What did Rav Sheshet say about dreaming that one killed a snake, and how does the Gemara evaluate his statement?
o: He said it means loss of livelihood, and the Gemara agrees
He said livelihood would double all the more, but the Gemara notes he said so because he himself had dreamed of killing a snake
He said it foretells death, and the Gemara rejects it
He said it is a sign of wisdom, and the Gemara accepts it
quiz.e: The tanna taught that killing the snake means losing one's livelihood; Rav Sheshet countered that it should double, but the Gemara remarks that Rav Sheshet had killed a snake in his own dream and wanted a positive reading.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara, a dream is one-sixtieth of what?
o: Death
The World-to-Come
Prophecy
Manna
quiz.e: Among five things that are one-sixtieth: fire of Gehenna, honey of manna, Shabbat of the World-to-Come, sleep of death, and a dream of prophecy.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, why must one say 'turn the hearts of their worshippers to serve You' even outside Eretz Yisrael?
o: Because idolatry is more common outside the Land
Because the nations are destined to convert, as in Zephaniah 3:9
Because the blessing formula may never be shortened
Because Rav Hamnuna requires five blessings on Babylonia
quiz.e: The Tosefta exempts one outside the Land since most inhabitants are gentiles, but Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar requires it because 'then I will turn to the peoples a pure language' foretells their conversion.
